pred_ddx.label: Lipomatous Hypertrophy of the Interatrial Septum

Atrial Myxoma: The patient's presentation with a large left atrial mass attached to the interatrial septum, prolapsing into the left ventricle, and obstructing the mitral valve orifice is consistent with the characteristic echocardiographic features and clinical manifestations of atrial myxomas. The size and location of the mass, as well as the patient's symptoms, support this diagnosis.
Lipomatous Hypertrophy of the Interatria: Although less likely, lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum is a possible diagnosis, given the patient's presentation with a left atrial mass attached to the interatrial septum. However, the size and shape of the mass, as well as the patient's symptoms, are not as consistent with this diagnosis as they are with atrial myxoma.
